Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Pramod Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Nikhil Srivastava, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA for the State.
3.

The instant second anticipatory bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.260 of 2023, under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 471, 507, 120-B IPC, Police Station Indirapuram, District Ghaziabad.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits however this is the second anticipatory bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and first anticipatory bail application of the applicant was dismissed vide order dated 02.02.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 CR.P.C. No.14525 of 2023 but the first anticipatory bail application of the applicant was dismissed on the ground that applicant challenged the FIR of the present case before Division Bench of this Court in criminal miscellaneous writ petition and writ petition filed by the applicant was still Alka Sharma vs State Of U.P. on 12 September, 2024

sentences.text:

1 pending and there was a direction that no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant and,
therefore, the first anticipatory bail application of the applicant has not been dismissed on merits and he is pressing the instant second anticipatory bail application on the ground that now the writ petition filed by the applicant has been dismissed by this Court on 07.06.2024.

5. At this stage, learned AGA as well as counsel for the informant pointed out that before filing of the instant second anticipatory bail application, process under Section 82 Cr.P.C. has been issued against the applicant on 03.06.2024 and, therefore, considering the observation made by the Apex Court in the case of Srikant Upadhyay and others Vs. State of Bihar and another 2024 SCC OnLIne SC 282, applicant is not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail and instant second anticipatory bail application should be dismissed on this sole ground even without touching merits of the case.

entities.text: Srikant Upadhyay and others Vs. State of Bihar and another 2024 SCC OnLIne SC 282
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They further submitted that applicant did not even comply the earlier order passed by the Division Bench of this Court and did not deposit the amount as directed by this Court.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant however submitted that all the other accused persons have been released on anticipatory bail even by the court concerned but could not dispute the fact that on 03.06.2024 process under Section 82 Cr.P.C. has been issued against the applicant and he did not comply the order passed by the Division Bench of this Court, however, he further submitted that applicant is not an absconder.
7. I have heard both the parties on preliminary objection raised by the learned AGA as well as counsel for the informant and perused the record of the case.

8. From the record, it reflects that this is the second anticipatory bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and first anticipatory bail application of the applicant has been dismissed by this Court but it reflects that first anticipatory bail application was not dismissed on merits and it was dismissed on the ground that applicant challenged the FIR of the present case before this Court in criminal misc. writ petition and at the time of hearing of first anticipatory bail application of the applicant, the criminal misc. writ petition filed by the applicant was pending and during the pendency of the criminal misc. writ petition, the matter was referred to the Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court and this Court directed that no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant 9.

It reflects that subsequently, the writ petition filed by the applicant was dismissed and thereafter,
the instant second anticipatory bail application was filed on 12.07.2024 but it appears that even before filling of the instant second anticipatory bail application on 03.06.2024, process under Section 82 Cr.P.C. has been issued against the applicant, therefore, it reflects that applicant was trying to evade his arrest and at this stage it cannot be said that he was not an absconder and,
therefore, considering the observation made by the Apex Court in the case of Srikant Upadhyay (supra), this court finds merit in the submission advanced by learned AGA as well as counsel for the informant that considering these facts even without touching merits of the case, the instant second anticipatory bail application is liable to be dismissed.
10.
Accordingly, the instant second anticipatory bail application is dismissed.
